Investors are witnessing growth rates typically seen in the early stages of an economic recovery, not 4 long years into a record-setting [bull market](https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/smart-money/bull-market). Earnings are growing so strongly that, relative to past tech stock rallies, [price-to-earnings (P/E)](https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/pe-ratio) valuations have been reasonable, even among the [Magnificent 7](http://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/smart-money/magnificent-7-stocks) mega-cap technology leaders. On the other hand, if energy supplies remain stressed and [oil prices](https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/us-iran-oil-prices) stay north of $100 a barrel, the damage could spill over to stocks and bonds because interest rates and consumer prices may be pushed higher. Another step might be to diversify into assets not correlated with either stocks or bonds, such as [commodities](https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/investment-products/mutual-funds/about-commodity-investing), especially energy. The [energy sector](https://www.fidelity.com/sector-investing/energy/overview) may be suitable for investors who believe the market has been complacent about the Iran situation and is underestimating the potential for oil prices to remain high. * [Analyzing stock fundamentals](https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/fundamental-analysis/analyzing-stock-fundamentals). * [Finding stock and sector ideas](https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/trading-investing/finding-stocks-and-sector-ideas). * [Stocks](https://www.fidelity.com/learning-center/investment-products/stocks/stocks).
